protocol.description:
The permission_authentication protocol allows to request user-interactable permission popups.
This protocol must be guarded behind the "core.unobtainium.tavernkeep" permission.
Its provider must be the permission barmaid started and authenticated by the tavern over its private startup channel. The tavern must not accept permission decisions from an arbitrary provider discovered by protocol name. The provider must authenticate the tavern's internal authority before accepting transactions; ordinary permission bypass does not confer that authority.
permission_authentication is an exclusive protocol. It must be exposed with the exclusivity flag.
The rules of hp_hyprtavern_core_v1 for unknown enum values apply.

value.name: invalid_argument
value.description: a malformed argument, e.g. an out-of-range enum value or a mismatched identity

value.name: invalid_state
value.description: a request out of the transaction's order

value.name: invalid_permission
value.description: a permission that cannot be prompted for

value.name: session
value.description: Until the requesting permission context ends

value.name: persist
value.description: Allow the user to choose a persistent or session grant

value.name: accepted_once
value.description: Accepted for this permission context's session, not a single operation

value.name: accepted_persistent
value.description: User consented to persistence; the tavern must still store the grant

value.name: unknown
value.description: no application identity could be attested

value.name: host_executable
value.description: identity is an attested executable of a verified same-user, unsandboxed host process

value.name: flatpak
value.description: identity is an attested Flatpak application ID

value.name: internal
value.description: identity is assigned by the tavern to an internal application

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_permission_authentication_manager_v1
object.description: This object is a core manager object bound upon creation.

s2c.name: availability

description.summary: Availability of the permission authentication manager

s2c.description:
This event is emitted on bind, and every time this changes.
The event describes whether asking for permissions is available. Certain things (e.g. DISPLAY / WAYLAND_DISPLAY env) can enable / disable the prompts from being shown.

c2s.name: request_availability
c2s.description: Request the current permission-prompt availability. The manager responds with an availability event.

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_permission_authentication_transaction_v1
object.description:
This object represents a permission transaction.
Identity setters are allowed only before ask_permission. That request freezes all inputs; only destroy is allowed thereafter, including while awaiting the result. Violating this order is an invalid_state protocol error.

c2s.name: set_requesting_app_display_name

description.summary: Set the requesting app's display name

c2s.description:
Set the human-readable application name shown for this transaction. This is display metadata and must not be treated as an attested identity.
This optional label must be presented as untrusted application-supplied text, without interpreting markup or control sequences or obscuring the attested identity. Omitting it must not prevent a prompt using the attested identity.

c2s.name: set_requesting_app_attested_id

description.summary: Set the requesting app's attested identifier

c2s.description:
Set the non-human-readable application identifier attested by the tavern for this transaction. Because only a client with core.unobtainium.tavernkeep may bind this protocol, this value is trusted agent metadata rather than an application self-assertion.
This request is required before ask_permission. identity_kind has the same meaning as in the core protocol and is part of the identifier's namespace. For unknown identity, attested_app_id must be empty and the UI must explicitly identify the requester as unknown rather than treating its display name as verified. Other identity kinds require a nonempty identifier.

arg.name: identity_kind
arg.summary: kind of the attested application identifier

c2s.name: ask_permission
c2s.description:
Ask the user for a permission. This may be done only once, after setting the attested identity. The permission must be promptable under the Hyprtavern permission catalog; core.unobtainium.unsandboxed and core.unobtainium.tavernkeep must never be prompted for. A permission that cannot be prompted for is an invalid_permission protocol error, and other invalid input is an invalid_argument one.
The displayed identity, permission, and offered lifetime must match this frozen transaction. A session request must not offer persistent approval; a persist request may offer either session or persistent approval. The tavern must request session when a stable owner or persistence is unavailable.
Exactly one permission_result follows unless the transaction is destroyed or the connection closes. If prompting is unavailable or becomes unavailable while pending, return unavailable rather than leaving the transaction pending.

s2c.name: permission_result
s2c.description:
Response from the manager with the result. permission_name must exactly match ask_permission. accepted_persistent is valid only for a persist request. accepted_once authorizes a session grant, not one service operation.
The tavern must apply the result only to the original requesting context and frozen transaction. A mismatched name or invalid lifetime is a protocol error and must not result in a grant. Persistent consent is not proof of a durable write: the tavern must persist the grant before reporting it as permanent through the core protocol.
This object may not be reused, you must not call anything that isn't destroy after this event.

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description: Destroys this transaction and dismisses any pending prompt without granting permission. No result is sent after destruction is processed. A result already sent may race with cancellation; the tavern must ignore it if its requesting context has already been destroyed or become unavailable.
